narrative: Material PL1__M3883975 shows erratic, intermittent demand (CV=1.43, 53.8% non-zero days) consistent with a compound-Poisson process, combined with highly unstable lead times (CV=0.94, mean 1.74 days). The current SAP policy using bare MOQ replenishment (308 units, ~104 orders/year) is operationally expensive; consolidating to EOQ-sized orders of 1,695 units (~19/year) reduces total annual inventory cost by 56.1%. Safety stock must be raised from 171 to 495 units (robust IQR method) to credibly protect a 95% service level against the demand and lead-time volatility observed.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic intermittent demand with unstable lead times requires a continuous monitoring trigger (reorder point r=931) to respond promptly to demand spikes, paired with a fixed EOQ order size (Q=1,695) that balances ordering and holding costs. Periodic review would add unnecessary exposure given the high demand variability.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage utilisation at 46.2% (2,190 of 4,741 units). Capacity does not constrain the EOQ; no service or cost degradation from the storage limit.
